name: Vyatka
notes: The Vyatskaya loshad, out of the Vyatka river basin around Kirov and into Udmurtia and Perm Krai: one of Russia's oldest native horses, shaped by forest, marshy meadow, snow, poor forage and long winter journeys by sledge. A village horse, not a stud creation.

Dun is the signature and it is real TBX3 dun, not a stripe painted on: D sits at the measured 0.30, so bay dun, savrasaya and mouse dun or grullo are the common outcomes, with d1 carried widely for primitive marking without body dilution.

Cream is deliberately present at a modest rate. The Vyatka colour-marker work notes that dun-plus-cream horses are commercially sought, which is how a dunskin or a smoky grullo gets to be a Vyatka rather than a mistake.

PSSM1 is the one seeded disorder and it is seeded high: a Vyatka population-genomic study reports the GYS1 allele at 0.189, which is about 31% heterozygous and 3.6% homozygous. The homozygous share is written into the founder pool deliberately - PSSM1 is dominant, so a heterozygote is affected rather than a silent carrier, and a third of the breed being genetically positive is what the measurement says rather than something to soften.
Everything else clear. Grey, pearl, champagne, silver, mushroom, every pinto pattern and the leopard complex are forced wild; sabino and rabicano sit at a trace for ordinary markings.
Cold tolerant near-fixed, which is the strongest tier here and the least arguable - this is a horse that works through a Kirov winter.
Winter coat, thick mane and tail, hoof hardness, forage thrift, the fast working trot and the line structure of the conservation programme are none of them modelled.
